images.alt: A bright brass lamp sheltered inside a stone arch as curved lines suggest wind outside
images.caption: The steady flame recalls the image in Bhagavad Gita 6.19.
images.prompt: An original devotional illustration in warm vermilion and deep indigo. Center a plain brass oil lamp with a steady flame in a sheltered stone niche while curved wind lines move outside the arch.

images.sectionHeading: What is abhyāsa in the Bhagavad Gita?
images.alt: Curving paths of attention arc outward and return toward a single light, illustrating Gita 6.26
images.caption: Verse 6.26 describes returning the mind whenever it wanders.
images.prompt: An original explanatory illustration in lapis blue and pale gold. Show several curved trajectories drifting outward before returning toward one luminous point, a visual interpretation of the recurring movement in verse 6.26.

images.sectionHeading: How practice and dispassion work together
images.alt: Two paths labeled practice and dispassion meet at a steady flame
images.caption: Practice returns attention. Dispassion weakens the pull away from it.
images.prompt: An original diagram with two legible labels, Practice and Dispassion, entering from opposite sides and meeting before a steady lamp. Use warm gold against a deep plum background and leave clear space around each label.
